record.paper_title: (E,E′N) and (E,E′NN) Experiments at NIKHEF, Mainz and JLab and Open Problems in One- and Two-Nucleon Emissions
record.original_question: Can precise exclusive 16O(e,e′pp) measurements to selected 14C final states, especially transitions dominated by knockout of a relative 1S0 proton pair, be used to determine short-range correlation functions tightly enough to constrain the off-shell behavior of the nucleon-nucleon potential? The unresolved issue is whether sufficiently accurate data in correlation-favored kinematics can distinguish among competing correlation models through their different predictions for these state-resolved cross sections.

evidence.quote: Such transitions are therefore most sensitive to short-range correlations.

As the calculations give significantly different results for different correlation functions, precise data could give important constraint when modelling the off-shell behavior of the nucleon-nucleon potential.
The data are still preliminary and require further analysis before a fully reliable comparison with calculations can be done.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the exclusive electron-induced two-proton knockout reaction $^{16}\mathrm{O}(e,e'pp)^{14}\mathrm{C}$, in which an incoming electron scatters from an $^{16}\mathrm{O}$ target and two protons are detected in coincidence with the scattered electron, leaving the residual nucleus $^{14}\mathrm{C}$ in a specific discrete final state (ground state or low-lying excited states). For kinematics that favor sensitivity to short-range correlations (small center-of-mass momentum of the pp pair, moderate energy and momentum transfer, with the pair predominantly in a relative ${}^1S_0$ state), the state-resolved differential cross section depends on (i) the two-nucleon overlap (spectroscopic) amplitudes for the transition, (ii) the central short-range correlation function $g(r)$ used to defect the relative pair wave function, (iii) tensor and other induced correlations, and (iv) two-body currents including meson-exchange and intermediate $\Delta$-isobar contributions.

Question: Can exclusive cross-section measurements of $^{16}\mathrm{O}(e,e'pp)^{14}\mathrm{C}$ to selected final states—especially those transitions dominated by knockout of a relative ${}^1S_0$ proton pair—be performed with sufficient precision in correlation-favored kinematics to:

(a) discriminate among competing models of the central nucleon-nucleon short-range correlation function $g(r)$ through their distinct predictions for these state-resolved cross sections; and

(b) thereby place quantitative constraints on the off-shell behavior of the nucleon-nucleon potential?

Specifically, determine whether achievable experimental precision and theoretical control (including treatment of final-state interactions, two-body currents, and competing reaction mechanisms) allow the state-resolved cross sections to uniquely fix $g(r)$ to within a tolerance that translates into a meaningful constraint on the off-shell $NN$ interaction.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent measurements and analyses (e.g., MAMI/Mainz high-resolution data and microscopic calculations including central SRC and Δ excitations) have demonstrated that the $^{16}$O(e,e′pp)$^{14}$C ground-state transition is indeed dominated by knockout of $^1S_0$ pp pairs and carries clear SRC signatures, with parameter-free calculations reproducing data. However, conclusively distinguishing among competing correlation functions to the point of tightly constraining the off-shell behavior of the NN potential has not been firmly established; results so far provide evidence for SRCs and qualitative discrimination but not a definitive off-shell constraint.

status_evidence.title: Signatures for short-range correlations in 16O observed in 16O(e,e'pp)14C
status_evidence.snippet: Cross sections to the 14C ground state are well reproduced by parameter-free microscopic calculations; the reaction is dominated by 1S0 pp knockout driven by short-range correlations.
status_evidence.claim: State-resolved measurements show clear SRC signatures dominated by 1S0 pair knockout.

status_evidence.title: The 16O(e,e'pp)14C reaction to discrete final states
status_evidence.snippet: Distorted-wave calculations including central SRC and Δ+ excitations are compared with MAMI high-resolution data at ω=215 MeV, q=316 MeV, providing additional evidence that SRCs affect pairs with small c.m. momentum in a relative S state.
status_evidence.claim: Microscopic calculations and data agree, supporting SRC interpretation but not yet uniquely fixing g(r).

status_evidence.title: Probing short-range correlations in 3He and 16O using (e,e'pp)
status_evidence.snippet: Review of probing SRCs via (e,e'pp) reactions on 3He and 16O.
status_evidence.claim: Active program established; off-shell NN constraints remain an open issue.
